body:
## Why

`hkb create --body "<!-- kb: {...} --> ## Why …"` prepends its own machine block and leaves the one
already in the text, so the card ends up with two. Nothing says so.

`parseBodyBlock` (`src/model.js:354`) is `^`-anchored, so the **first** block is the card's real
config and the second is inert body text — no misdispatch. The cost is that the two are byte-identical
in shape, so a reader cannot tell which one governs:

- `hkb show <n>` prints the rest-of-body, stray block included, right where a machine block belongs.
  On 2026-09-03 the operator seat read `{"priority":2}` off `hkb show 294`, concluded the card carried
  no `model`, and was one step from re-dispatching a running A6 onto the wrong model. The real block
  said `"model":"claude-opus-5"` all along.
- `hkb context` puts the body in the worker's brief, so the worker reads a config block that governs
  nothing.
- `serializeBodyBlock(kb, rest)` re-emits `rest` verbatim, so every later write preserves the stray
  copy. It never self-heals.
- The two drift the moment anything edits the real one: `hkb edit 294 --priority 3` moves the first
  block and leaves the second saying `2`.

Measured on this board: 16 of 17 track cards carried a duplicate (every card filed by a
materializer script that emitted a body already containing a block); the one filed by hand had one.
They were stripped by hand on 2026-09-03 — this card is about hkb not producing them.

## What

1. `create` (and `edit`/anything else taking `--body`) detects a leading `<!-- kb: … -->` in the
   supplied text. **Absorb it**: parse it, merge under the explicit flags (a `--priority` on the
   command line wins over the body's), and emit exactly one block. Round-tripping a card body —
   `hkb show` → edit → `hkb create` — is the obvious workflow and it should just work (value 4).
2. A block that is *not* at the top of the supplied body is the ambiguous case: refuse with exit 2
   naming the line, rather than guessing which one the author meant.
3. A malformed block in supplied text refuses too — today `parseBodyBlock` turns it into
   `_malformed: true` and carries on, which is right for reading a card that is already on the board
   and wrong for accepting new input.
4. `hkb doctor` reports cards carrying more than one block, since existing boards have them and
   nothing else will ever notice.

## Done when

- [ ] `hkb create --body` with a leading block yields one block, with flags winning over body keys.
- [ ] A non-leading or malformed block in supplied text exits 2 naming what to fix.
- [ ] `hkb doctor` flags multi-block cards.
- [ ] Tests for each, including the round-trip (`show` → `create`).
- [ ] `npm run lint && npm test` green.
title: hkb create --body silently leaves two kb blocks on a card, and only the first one governs
